--- title: Market Baseline bibliography: references.bib csl: csl/apa.csl format: html: code-fold: true code-summary: Show my code execute: freeze: auto warning: false --- ## Introduction For this market baseline, we are using job-posting data from Computer Systems Design and Related Services industry (NAICS 5415). We look at job titles, locations, work arrangements, salaries, and analytics tools mentioned in the job descriptions. This will help us understand the opportunities shown in our data and give us a starting point for comparing them with our team’s skills. We began by checking how much data we have and what information is available. We then looked at missing values, converted usable salary ranges into annual amounts, and created charts to make the patterns easier to understand. We found some limitations along the way, including missing location information, unknown work arrangements, and roles outside our intended analytics focus. ## Dataset overview ::: {#042ad08f .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from pyspark.sql import SparkSession from pyspark.sql import functions as F spark = SparkSession.builder \ .appName("AD688_JobFacts") \ .config("spark.sql.session.timeZone", "UTC") \ .getOrCreate() spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("ERROR") jobs_clean = spark.read.csv( "./outputs/api_job_facts_cleaned.csv", header=True, inferSchema=True, multiLine=True, escape='"' ) # use this clean table for all downstream analysis jobs_clean.createOrReplaceTempView("job_facts") spark.sql("SELECT COUNT(*) AS row_count FROM job_facts").show() spark.sql("SELECT * FROM job_facts LIMIT 50").toPandas() ``` ::: ::: {#9c5db403 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} jobs_clean.printSchema() jobs_clean.groupBy("normalized_title").count().orderBy(F.desc("count")).show(30, truncate=False) ``` ::: ::: {#72811a69 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} baseline_summary = spark.sql(""" SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_postings, COUNT(DISTINCT job_id) AS unique_job_ids, COUNT(DISTINCT company_name) AS distinct_employers, MIN(posted_at) AS earliest_posting, MAX(posted_at) AS latest_posting FROM job_facts """) baseline_summary.toPandas().T.rename(columns={0: "Value"}) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
Value
total_postings 2353
unique_job_ids 2353
distinct_employers 1506
earliest_posting 2026-05-25 00:00:00
latest_posting 2026-08-07 00:00:00
``` ::: ::: ::: {#7e828790 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} top_employers = spark.sql(""" SELECT company_name, COUNT(*) AS postings FROM job_facts WHERE company_name IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(company_name) <> '' GROUP BY company_name ORDER BY postings DESC, company_name LIMIT 15 """) top_employers.show(truncate=False) ``` ::: ::: {#825200e7 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} top_roles = spark.sql(""" SELECT COALESCE( NULLIF(TRIM(normalized_title), ''), TRIM(title) ) AS role_title, COUNT(*) AS postings FROM job_facts GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY postings DESC, role_title LIMIT 20 """) top_roles.show(20, truncate=False) ``` ::: ## Location coverage ::: {#d7944286 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} top_locations = spark.sql(""" SELECT COALESCE( NULLIF(TRIM(location_text), ''), 'Unknown' ) AS location, COUNT(*) AS postings FROM job_facts GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY postings DESC, location LIMIT 20 """) top_locations.toPandas() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: {#4054b44d .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} location_check = spark.sql(""" SELECT location_text, city, state, state_code FROM job_facts WHERE location_text IS NULL OR TRIM(location_text) = '' OR LOWER(TRIM(location_text)) = 'unknown' LIMIT 20 """) location_check.show(20, truncate=False) ``` ::: ::: {#6188b82a .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} spark.sql(""" SELECT COUNT(*) AS unknown_location_postings, COUNT(NULLIF(TRIM(city), '')) AS with_city, COUNT(NULLIF(TRIM(state), '')) AS with_state, COUNT(NULLIF(TRIM(state_code), '')) AS with_state_code FROM job_facts WHERE location_text IS NULL OR TRIM(location_text) = '' OR LOWER(TRIM(location_text)) = 'unknown' """).toPandas().T.rename(columns={0: "Value"}) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=8} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: {#adec4d66 .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} work_arrangements = spark.sql(""" WITH counts AS ( SELECT COALESCE( NULLIF(TRIM(remote_status), ''), 'Unknown' ) AS work_arrangement, COUNT(*) AS postings FROM job_facts GROUP BY 1 ) SELECT work_arrangement, postings, ROUND( 100.0 * postings / SUM(postings) OVER (), 1 ) AS percent_of_postings FROM counts ORDER BY postings DESC """) work_arrangements.show(truncate=False) ``` ::: ## Salary coverage and currency checks ::: {#03233571 .cell execution_count=10} ``` {.python .cell-code} salary_coverage = spark.sql(""" SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_postings, SUM(CASE WHEN annual_salary_min IS NOT NULL AND annual_salary_max IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS with_annual_range, SUM(CASE WHEN hourly_salary_min IS NOT NULL AND hourly_salary_max IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS with_hourly_range, SUM(CASE WHEN annual_salary_min IS NULL AND annual_salary_max IS NULL AND hourly_salary_min IS NULL AND hourly_salary_max IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS without_numeric_salary FROM job_facts """) salary_coverage.toPandas().T.rename(columns={0: "Value"}) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=10} ```{=html}
Value
total_postings 2353
with_annual_range 458
with_hourly_range 45
without_numeric_salary 1850
``` ::: ::: ::: {#bc010ea4 .cell execution_count=11} ``` {.python .cell-code} spark.sql(""" SELECT title, location_text, salary_text, annual_salary_min, annual_salary_max FROM job_facts WHERE annual_salary_min IS NOT NULL AND annual_salary_max IS NOT NULL ORDER BY location_text, job_id LIMIT 20 """).show(20, truncate=100) ``` ::: ::: {#fee42eae .cell execution_count=12} ``` {.python .cell-code} from pyspark.sql import functions as F has_annual = ( F.col("annual_salary_min").isNotNull() & F.col("annual_salary_max").isNotNull() ) has_hourly = ( F.col("hourly_salary_min").isNotNull() & F.col("hourly_salary_max").isNotNull() ) currency_code = F.regexp_extract( F.upper(F.coalesce(F.col("salary_text"), F.lit(""))), r"\b(USD|CAD|EUR|GBP|AUD|NZD|INR|SGD|JPY|CHF|CNY|AED)\b", 1 ) jobs_pay = ( jobs_clean .withColumn( "annualized_min", F.when(has_annual, F.col("annual_salary_min")) .when(has_hourly, F.col("hourly_salary_min") * 2080) ) .withColumn( "annualized_max", F.when(has_annual, F.col("annual_salary_max")) .when(has_hourly, F.col("hourly_salary_max") * 2080) ) .withColumn( "salary_basis", F.when(has_annual, "Reported annual") .when(has_hourly, "Hourly converted × 2080") .otherwise("No complete range") ) .withColumn( "salary_currency", F.when(currency_code != "", currency_code) .otherwise("Unconfirmed") ) ) jobs_pay.filter(F.col("annualized_min").isNotNull()) \ .groupBy("salary_currency", "salary_basis").count() \ .orderBy(F.desc("count")) \ .show(truncate=False) ``` ::: ::: {#1ae6b271 .cell execution_count=13} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Identify US locations from country labels or state abbreviations. us_states = ( "AL|AK|AZ|AR|CA|CO|CT|DE|FL|GA|HI|ID|IL|IN|IA|KS|KY|LA|" "ME|MD|MA|MI|MN|MS|MO|MT|NE|NV|NH|NJ|NM|NY|NC|ND|OH|OK|" "OR|PA|RI|SC|SD|TN|TX|UT|VT|VA|WA|WV|WI|WY|DC" ) location = F.upper(F.coalesce(F.col("location_text"), F.lit(""))) us_location = ( location.rlike(r"\bUNITED STATES\b|\bUSA\b|\bU\.S\.A?\.") | location.rlike(r",\s*(" + us_states + r")\b") | location.rlike( r"\b(ARIZONA|TEXAS|CALIFORNIA|FLORIDA|MARYLAND|" r"MICHIGAN|MISSOURI|NEW YORK)\b" ) | location.rlike(r"\bLOS ANGELES METROPOLITAN AREA\b") ) assume_usd = ( (F.col("salary_currency") == "Unconfirmed") & us_location ) jobs_pay = ( jobs_pay .withColumn( "currency_basis", F.when(assume_usd, "Assumed from US location") .when( F.col("salary_currency") != "Unconfirmed", "Explicit currency in salary text" ) .otherwise("Unconfirmed") ) .withColumn( "salary_currency", F.when(assume_usd, "USD") .otherwise(F.col("salary_currency")) ) ) jobs_pay.filter( F.col("annualized_min").isNotNull() ).groupBy( "salary_currency", "currency_basis" ).count().orderBy(F.desc("count")).toPandas() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=13} ```{=html}
salary_currency currency_basis count
0 USD Assumed from US location 238
1 USD Explicit currency in salary text 203
2 Unconfirmed Unconfirmed 39
3 CAD Explicit currency in salary text 20
4 EUR Explicit currency in salary text 2
5 GBP Explicit currency in salary text 1
``` ::: ::: ::: {#b5a041d9 .cell execution_count=14} ``` {.python .cell-code} usd_pay = ( jobs_pay .filter( (F.col("salary_currency") == "USD") & F.col("annualized_min").isNotNull() & F.col("annualized_max").isNotNull() ) .withColumn( "annual_midpoint", (F.col("annualized_min") + F.col("annualized_max")) / 2 ) ) usd_pay.agg( F.count("*").alias("postings"), F.round( F.percentile_approx("annual_midpoint", 0.5), 2 ).alias("median_annual_midpoint_usd"), F.round( F.avg("annual_midpoint"), 2 ).alias("mean_annual_midpoint_usd") ).show(truncate=False) ``` ::: ::: {#e80bc310 .cell execution_count=15} ``` {.python .cell-code} jobs_pay.filter( (F.col("annualized_min").isNotNull()) & (F.col("salary_currency") == "Unconfirmed") ).select( "location_text", "salary_text", "salary_basis" ).orderBy( "location_text", "salary_text" ).show(30, truncate=100) ``` ::: ::: {#e0afc2ea .cell execution_count=16} ``` {.python .cell-code} usd_role_pay = ( usd_pay .withColumn( "role", F.coalesce( F.when( F.trim(F.col("normalized_title")) != "", F.trim(F.col("normalized_title")) ), F.trim(F.col("title")) ) ) .groupBy("role") .agg( F.count("*").alias("salary_postings"), F.round( F.percentile_approx("annual_midpoint", 0.5), 2 ).alias("median_annual_midpoint_usd") ) .filter(F.col("salary_postings") >= 5) .orderBy(F.desc("salary_postings"), "role") ) usd_role_pay.show(20, truncate=False) ``` ::: ## Checking the structured skills data ::: {#fb158c49 .cell execution_count=17} ``` {.python .cell-code} jobs_clean.filter( F.col("skills").isNotNull() & (F.trim(F.col("skills")) != "") & (F.trim(F.col("skills")) != "[]") ).select( "title", "skills" ).show(5, truncate=False) ``` ::: ::: {#b3d8ae4c .cell execution_count=18} ``` {.python .cell-code} skills_parsed = jobs_clean.withColumn( "skills_array", F.from_json( F.col("skills"), "array>" ) ) # Check how many postings have usable skill information. skills_parsed.agg( F.count("*").alias("total_postings"), F.sum( F.when(F.size("skills_array") > 0, 1).otherwise(0) ).alias("postings_with_skills") ).show(truncate=False) # Extract skill names and count distinct postings. job_skills = ( skills_parsed .select("job_id", F.explode("skills_array").alias("skill_record")) .select( "job_id", F.lower(F.trim(F.col("skill_record.name"))).alias("skill") ) .filter(F.col("skill").isNotNull() & (F.col("skill") != "")) .dropDuplicates(["job_id", "skill"]) ) skill_demand = ( job_skills .groupBy("skill") .agg(F.countDistinct("job_id").alias("postings")) .orderBy(F.desc("postings"), "skill") ) skill_demand.show(20, truncate=False) ``` ::: ::: {#49e0f9c8 .cell execution_count=19} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Check how many skills the source stored per posting. skills_parsed.groupBy( F.size("skills_array").alias("skills_per_posting") ).count().orderBy("skills_per_posting").show(30, truncate=False) # Look for common analytics tools anywhere in the recorded skills. skill_demand.filter( F.col("skill").rlike( r"sql|python|tableau|power\s*bi|excel|" r"pandas|spark|statistics|visualization" ) ).show(50, truncate=False) ``` ::: ::: {#e5b5e26f .cell execution_count=20} ``` {.python .cell-code} job_skills.withColumn( "first_character", F.substring("skill", 1, 1) ).groupBy( "first_character" ).agg( F.countDistinct("skill").alias("distinct_skills"), F.count("*").alias("posting_skill_pairs") ).orderBy("first_character").toPandas() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=20} ```{=html}
first_character distinct_skills posting_skill_pairs
0 . 1 2
1 3 2 6
2 a 315 5056
3 b 161 3377
4 c 67 421
``` ::: ::: ::: {#652133f5 .cell execution_count=21} ``` {.python .cell-code} has_description = ( F.col("description").isNotNull() & (F.length(F.trim(F.col("description"))) > 0) ) jobs_clean.agg( F.count("*").alias("total_postings"), F.sum( F.when(has_description, 1).otherwise(0) ).alias("postings_with_description") ).show(truncate=False) jobs_clean.filter(has_description).select( "title", F.substring("description", 1, 500).alias("description_preview") ).show(3, truncate=False) ``` ::: ::: {#f5d839a0 .cell execution_count=22} ``` {.python .cell-code} tool_patterns = [ ("SQL", r"\bsql\b"), ("Python", r"\bpython\b"), ("Excel", r"\bexcel\b(?!\s+(?:in|at|as|within)\b)"), ("Tableau", r"\btableau\b"), ("Power BI", r"\bpower[\s-]*bi\b"), ("Apache Spark / PySpark", r"\b(?:apache\s+spark|pyspark)\b"), ("Pandas", r"\bpandas\b") ] description_jobs = jobs_clean.filter(has_description).withColumn( "description_lower", F.lower(F.col("description")) ) description_count = description_jobs.select("job_id").distinct().count() tool_mentions = ( description_jobs .select( "job_id", F.explode(F.array(*[ F.struct( F.lit(tool).alias("tool"), F.col("description_lower").rlike(pattern).alias("mentioned") ) for tool, pattern in tool_patterns ])).alias("match") ) .groupBy(F.col("match.tool").alias("tool")) .agg( F.countDistinct( F.when(F.col("match.mentioned"), F.col("job_id")) ).alias("postings_mentioning_tool") ) .withColumn( "percent_of_descriptions", F.round( F.col("postings_mentioning_tool") / description_count * 100, 1 ) ) .orderBy(F.desc("postings_mentioning_tool"), "tool") ) tool_mentions.show(truncate=False) ``` ::: ::: {#dabb8e9c .cell execution_count=23} ``` {.python .cell-code} description_jobs.filter( F.col("description_lower").rlike(r"\bexcel\b") ).select( "title", F.regexp_extract( F.col("description_lower"), r"(?s)(.{0,80}\bexcel\b.{0,80})", 1 ).alias("excel_context") ).show(10, truncate=False) ``` ::: ## Tools mentioned in job descriptions ::: {#3e7d2885 .cell execution_count=24} ``` {.python .cell-code} import plotly.express as px tool_chart_data = tool_mentions.toPandas().sort_values( "postings_mentioning_tool", ascending=False ) fig_tools = px.bar( tool_chart_data, x="postings_mentioning_tool", y="tool", orientation="h", text="postings_mentioning_tool", hover_data={"percent_of_descriptions": ":.1f"}, labels={ "postings_mentioning_tool": "Postings mentioning tool", "tool": "Tool", "percent_of_descriptions": "Descriptions (%)" }, title="Selected Analytics Tools Mentioned in Job Descriptions", template="plotly_white" ) fig_tools.update_yaxes( categoryorder="array", categoryarray=tool_chart_data["tool"].tolist(), autorange="reversed" ) fig_tools.update_traces( marker_color="#2563EB", textposition="outside", cliponaxis=False ) fig_tools.update_layout( height=450, margin=dict(l=30, r=70, t=80, b=50), xaxis=dict( range=[0, tool_chart_data["postings_mentioning_tool"].max() * 1.15] ) ) fig_tools.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: SQL and Python were the most frequently mentioned tools among the seven we checked, appearing in 38.3% and 35.8% of job descriptions. This gives us a starting point for comparing employer mentions with our team’s skills. We used descriptions because the structured skills field appeared incomplete. A mention does not always mean the tool is required. ::: {#896d9712 .cell execution_count=25} ``` {.python .cell-code} %pip install plotly nbformat ``` ::: ## Work arrangements ::: {#26bb9b97 .cell execution_count=26} ``` {.python .cell-code} work_chart_data = ( jobs_clean .groupBy("remote_status") .count() .toPandas() .sort_values("count", ascending=False) ) work_chart_data["percent"] = ( work_chart_data["count"] / work_chart_data["count"].sum() * 100 ).round(1) fig_work = px.bar( work_chart_data, x="remote_status", y="count", text="count", color="remote_status", color_discrete_map={ "Unknown": "#9CA3AF", "Hybrid": "#2563EB", "Remote": "#059669", "On-site": "#D97706" }, hover_data={"percent": ":.1f"}, labels={ "remote_status": "Work arrangement", "count": "Postings", "percent": "Postings (%)" }, title="Recorded Work Arrangements", template="plotly_white" ) fig_work.update_traces(textposition="outside", cliponaxis=False) fig_work.update_layout( showlegend=False, height=420, yaxis=dict(range=[0, work_chart_data["count"].max() * 1.15]) ) fig_work.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: Hybrid and remote postings were almost equal, with 518 hybrid and 510 remote roles, compared with 254 on-site roles. However, 1,071 postings, or 45.5%, had an unknown work arrangement. This limits how much we can conclude about work arrangements across the full sample. ## Most common job titles ::: {#3d7570fd .cell execution_count=27} ``` {.python .cell-code} role_chart_data = ( jobs_clean .withColumn( "role", F.coalesce( F.when( F.trim(F.col("normalized_title")) != "", F.trim(F.col("normalized_title")) ), F.trim(F.col("title")) ) ) .filter(F.col("role").isNotNull() & (F.col("role") != "")) .groupBy("role") .agg(F.countDistinct("job_id").alias("postings")) .orderBy(F.desc("postings"), "role") .limit(15) .toPandas() ) fig_roles = px.bar( role_chart_data, x="postings", y="role", orientation="h", text="postings", labels={"postings": "Postings", "role": "Recorded job title"}, title="Top 15 Recorded Job Titles", template="plotly_white" ) fig_roles.update_yaxes( categoryorder="array", categoryarray=role_chart_data["role"].tolist(), autorange="reversed" ) fig_roles.update_traces( marker_color="#2563EB", textposition="outside", cliponaxis=False ) fig_roles.update_layout( height=650, margin=dict(l=30, r=60, t=80, b=50), xaxis=dict(range=[0, role_chart_data["postings"].max() * 1.15]) ) fig_roles.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: This graph shows the most common recorded job titles in our current sample. We also found attorney and HR titles outside our intended analytics focus, which showed that the initial filter needs further review. The chart helps us understand what was collected, but we need a more focused sample before drawing conclusions about analytics opportunities. ## Annualized salary distribution ::: {#c5e3ea1d .cell execution_count=28} ``` {.python .cell-code} salary_chart_data = usd_pay.select("annual_midpoint").toPandas() salary_median = salary_chart_data["annual_midpoint"].median() fig_salary = px.histogram( salary_chart_data, x="annual_midpoint", nbins=30, labels={"annual_midpoint": "Annualized salary midpoint (USD)"}, title=f"Annualized Salary Midpoints ({len(salary_chart_data):,} Postings)", template="plotly_white" ) fig_salary.update_traces(marker_color="#2563EB") fig_salary.add_vline( x=salary_median, line_dash="dash", line_color="#D97706", annotation_text=f"Median: ${salary_median:,.0f}", annotation_position="top right" ) fig_salary.update_layout( height=450, xaxis_tickprefix="$", xaxis_tickformat=",", yaxis_title="Number of postings", bargap=0.05 ) fig_salary.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: For the 441 postings included in this salary analysis, the median annualized salary midpoint was $134,250. The distribution has a tail toward higher salaries, showing that some advertised ranges were much higher than others. These are advertised range midpoints rather than actual earnings, and the sample combines different roles and experience levels. Hourly salaries were converted using 2,080 hours per year, and some currencies were assumed to be USD.
